definition: In artificial intelligence, model-based reasoning refers to an inference method used in expert systems based on a model of the physical world.
details: With this approach, the main focus of application development is developing the model. Then at run time, an "engine" combines this model knowledge with observed data to derive conclusions such as a diagnosis or a prediction.
story: Imagine a mathematician who writes every step on paper, reads it back, crosses out a bad line, and starts that line over. Slowing down to think often beats answering fast. Instead of blurting out an answer, the machine talks its way through the problem one step at a time. More time spent reconsidering can be worth more than a bigger model. And that habit of thinking twice — or a hundred times — is Model-based reasoning.
